headline: Computational antibody and binder design diagnosed beyond raw structure predictions
label: Computational Antibody And Binder Design
summary: Recent work pairs agentic, language-model and structure-based design with diagnostic checks of binding, specificity and self-association.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluating computational binder and antibody designs against criteria beyond the raw prediction. The de novo SARS-CoV-2 RBD study combines AlphaFold, molecular dynamics, docking and SAP signatures to diagnose trade-offs between target binding and self-association, exposing failure modes in designed binders. Complementary work uses an antigen-specific protein language model to guide CDR optimization. New preprints extend design into multi-variant and agentic settings: Germinal Multi jointly optimizes one paratope against observed and forecasted antigen variants, yielding designs that bind EGFR variants and neutralize SARS-CoV-2, while Claude-enabled agentic design produces biparatopic IgE disruptors, three of which outperform omalizumab at removing bound IgE. The IgE work is less directly diagnostic, emphasizing comparative functional performance.
